chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Surely Allah commands you to render the trusts to their people.
He عليه السلام said: They are the Imams. The Imam hands it over to the Imam after him, and he does not single out anyone other than him with it, nor does he withhold it from him.

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: their rightful possessors, meaning those entitled to receive the trust
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, the designated bearers of divine authority
key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: the trusts, interpreted here as the entrusted authority and office of Imamate
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader in each generation
key_terms.مِنْ بَعْدِهِ: after him, referring to the succeeding Imam
key_terms.يَزْوِيهَا: he withholds it or turns it away
key_terms.يُؤَدِّي: he delivers or hands over, indicating transmission of the trust

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida عليه السلام interpret the verse about rendering trusts to their owners?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic command of rendering trusts as referring to the transmission of the divine trust of Imamate to its rightful possessors. It states that each Imam delivers it to the Imam after him alone, affirming the designated continuity of religious authority among the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[4:58] Surely Allah Commands you to make over trusts to their owners

. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They<sup>asws</sup> are the Imams<sup>asws</sup>. The Imam<sup>asws</sup> hands over the entrustments to the Imam<sup>asws</sup> to be from after him<sup>asws</sup>, and no one else is particularised with it apart from him<sup>asws</sup>, nor is it impeded from him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Fudayl from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) about the following words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High.
“Allah (God) commands you to return that which had been entrusted to you to the rightful owners. Be just when passing judgment among people. . .”

[4:58] The Imam (a.s.) said, “They are the Imams (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) must deliver the trust to the succeeding Imam (a.s.) exclusively and to no one else and that the succeeding Imams must not be deprived of this trust.”
